idiom_name: factory function returning a frozen object over closure state
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no constructor that can fail and no runtime privacy, so the factory function is the native creation idiom: validate the input, build and Object.freeze the returned object, and keep mutable state in the closure (or in #private fields of a class) so callers can reach it only through the behaviour you expose. What replaces the classic factory class is the module-scoped createOrder(...) function; classes remain relevant where a framework demands them, and even then construction should stay a named function that enforces the rules.
pitfalls: Object.freeze() is shallow: nested arrays and objects stay mutable, so copy or freeze each collection that arrives from the caller.
Closure state is unreachable but also uninspectable; expose readers for the properties the application needs instead of returning the raw state object.
Nothing in the language stops a caller from hand-building the same shape; the factory's authority rests on not exporting a class or constructor, and on validating at the boundary.
